description_full: Corning Incorporated operates in optical communications, display, specialty materials, automotive, and life sciences businesses in the United States, Canada, Mexico, Japan, Taiwan, China, South Korea, Germany, and internationally. The company provides optical fibers and cables; and hardware and equipment products, such as cable assemblies, fiber optic hardware and connectors, optical components and couplers, closures, network interface devices, and other accessories for the telecommunications industry, businesses, governments, and individuals. It also offers glass substrates for flat panel displays, including liquid crystal displays and organic light-emitting diodes that are used in televisions, notebook computers, desktop monitors, tablets, and handheld devices. In addition, it manufactures products that offer material formulations for glass, glass ceramics, crystals, precision metrology instruments, and software, as well as glass wafers and substrates, tinted sunglasses, and radiation shielding products for markets, such as mobile consumer electronics, semiconductor equipment optics and consumables, aerospace and defense optics, radiation shielding products, sunglasses, and telecommunications components. Further, the company provides ceramic substrates and filter products for emissions control in mobile, gasoline, and diesel applications, as well as technical glass and optic products and solutions for the interior and exterior of vehicles. Additionally, it offers laboratory products, including plastic vessels, liquid handling plastics, specialty surfaces, cell culture media, and serum, as well as general labware, and glassware and equipment under the Corning, Falcon, PYREX, and Axygen brands. It also offers polysilicon products and pharmaceutical glass tubing and vials. The company was formerly known as Corning Glass Works and changed its name to Corning Incorporated in April 1989. Corning Incorporated was founded in 1851 and is headquartered in Corning, New York.

financial_summary: Corning Incorporated is a large-cap technology business with a $98.3B market cap on $15.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +3% over the past three years and +6% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 6% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 40%.

The business throws off $1.4B in free cash flow — roughly 9 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.69× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 2.0× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 6.8×.
Shareholder yield is only 1.2%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 8.1% of the shares.

Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 168% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 1.4% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 2.1% (vs the 8% bar).

prof: ROIC of 6% falls short of the cost of capital of 9.5%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.41).

Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.69x.

hlth: Leverage is moderate at 2.0x net debt to EBITDA ($1.5B of cash against $8.4B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 6.8x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 4.8, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 3.3% over 3 years, 6.7% over 5 years and 5.5% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
At current returns, reinvesting 14% of profits supports about 0.8% a year of fundamental growth, too little to drive meaningful growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 12.0% a year over five years.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.0x, 8.2% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 14, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 8.1%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 74%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (6 sales, net $33.4M sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.2% (0.2% in buybacks and 1.0% in dividends).

That works out to $21K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $11.5M (49x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (8/10, lower is better).
